title: Semiparametric Efficiency for Conditional Optimal Transport Bounds in Observational Studies
banked_reason: Independent referee re-grade: subfield, not field. The headline efficiency/DML theorem is the propensity-corrected version of Lin-Gao-Blanchet-Glynn arXiv:2602.20681 (Prop 3.3 + Thm 3.2: same conditional estimand, same centered-Kantorovich-potential influence function, same s > D/2 condition; cited by the note) composed with Manole et al. AoS 2024 Lemma 21/Thm 22, i.e. exactly the one-step correction the cited literature names as its own future work; the single open question (degeneracy-adaptive inference) is unresolved.
gap_reasons: The degeneracy theorem proves only that one unregularized full-tangent Gaussian spectral construction fails at an admissible identity-compression witness, while honest full-parent adaptation remains open.

The framing overclaims necessity when it says covariate regularization, a uniform Hilbert-Schmidt tail, and uniform estimation of the regularized Hessian are all necessary: the proofs establish the generic Gaussian-series criterion and failure of the unregularized route, not a necessity theorem covering every regularized spectral calibration.
The claimed phase boundaries are sufficient for the chosen finite-net/DML construction and have no converse, as the note ultimately acknowledges.

The headline theorem is the one-step correction that the run's own closest comparator names as its future work. Lin-Gao-Blanchet-Glynn arXiv:2602.20681 — cited here as lin2026statistical — already contains, for the SAME conditional estimand: Prop 3.3 (the signed one-sided second-order remainder, = lem:two-sample-quadratic-remainder), Thm 3.2 (root-n normality with centered conditional Kantorovich potentials under 2s > d_Y + d_Z, = this note's influence function and its s > D/2 condition verbatim), and Remark 3.2 (the equality-degeneracy case). What they lack is the propensity score and the word 'efficient'; the note supplies exactly those two.
The companion paper arXiv:2502.01164 (cited as lin2025tightening) states in its own future work: 'A potential approach is using the one-step correction estimator from the semi-parametric literature.'

The efficiency half is Manole et al. AoS 2024 composed one step: their Lemma 21 gives the centered Kantorovich potential as the efficient influence function of W_2^2, their Thm 22 gives matching one- and two-sample LAM lower bounds. The run itself quotes both verbatim in core.json as lem:manole-unconditional-smooth-wasserstein-efficiency.

Presentation inverts the content: def:conditional-transport-pathwise-differentiability POSITS the derivative formula as a property D(P), and thm:abstract-observed-canonical-gradient then proves the headline in eight lines of centering algebra given D. The real work — deriving D by an envelope/Danskin argument — sits in lem:integrated-arm-path-differentiation, a lemma.

ass:uniform-conditional-brenier-{smoothness,lower,upper} are labelled 'Standard (uniform A1-type, manole2024plugin)' but Manole's A1 is a per-pair POPULATION hypothesis; quantifying it over an entire nonparametric class is what makes the stability lemma uniform, and every rate in the note rides on that. Worse, the condition involves no P at all yet is listed as a member property of the parent law class, so if it fails the class is empty and every theorem is vacuous. Non-vacuity is never established for d_Y >= 2.

The spectral obstruction is generic, not transport-specific: in lem:conditional-hessian-spectral-obstruction the perturbation is a product e(x)g(y) with g FIXED, giving a constant ratio for every e. It is the statement that a fibrewise quadratic form averaged over a nonatomic covariate law has an eigenvalue of infinite multiplicity, and would hold identically for a plain squared-difference functional. Nothing about Brenier potentials is used.

Uncited comparator: Agarwal-Luedtke, 'Sinkhorn Treatment Effects', arXiv:2605.08485 (May 2026) — first-order EIF of the form (centered entropic dual potential)/propensity, debiased estimators, and at equality a proof that the first-order EIF vanishes with a weighted chi-square second-order limit. That is the structure of both the efficiency claim and the degeneracy analysis, published two months before this run.
The proposal-stage gate recorded published_axis_verdict 'clear' with papers_verified 8, and state.json shows 'field' asserted at iterations 0-6 without ever being re-tested against delivered content.
proof_attempt_summary: Aimed at the semiparametric efficiency bound and honest inference for the optimal-transport lower bound on the average squared individual treatment effect, in an OBSERVATIONAL design. What was delivered is the influence function (a covariate term plus the centered conditional Kantorovich dual potential over the propensity), a cross-fitted debiased estimator attaining it, and Wald validity including along sequences with vanishing variance — which is the published randomized-design theory of Lin-Gao-Blanchet-Glynn composed with Manole et al.'s unconditional efficiency result and a propensity correction, i.e. exactly the one-step correction the cited literature names as its own future work. The single open question, inference at the degenerate boundary where the two arms coincide, was not solved: what was proved there is that ONE unregularized Gaussian spectral route fails, via a mechanism that is generic to fibrewise quadratic forms and uses nothing about transport.
tldr: Smooth conditional-optimal-transport inference already includes the wavelet stability and randomized marginal-sample asymptotic normality of Lin--Gao--Blanchet--Glynn. For the sharp lower endpoint on mean squared individual treatment effects, this note establishes three different observational results: the covariate-composition plus inverse-propensity canonical gradient under ignorability and overlap; the semiparametric information lower bound together with a propensity-corrected cross-fitted one-step estimator that attains it; and uniform studentized normality and Wald coverage on admissible positive-variance collections, including \(\sigma_n\to0\), under \(\sqrt n\,\delta_n/\sigma_n\to0\), \(r_{S,n}/\sigma_n\to0\), and \(\sqrt n\,\sigma_n\to\infty\). At equality, the first-order pivot fails and the unregularized full-tangent Gaussian spectral route is obstructed by a noncompact, non-Hilbert--Schmidt Hessian; an honest full-parent adaptive procedure using controlled regularization or a different calibration remains open.
gap: Lin--Gao--Blanchet--Glynn already provide smooth-density wavelet conditional-optimal-transport stability and pointwise asymptotic normality for randomized marginal samples. Their theorem does not provide the observational tangent-space gradient with both covariate-composition and inverse-propensity terms, an information lower bound with an attaining observational estimator, or uniform studentized coverage along admissible sequences with \(\sigma_n\to0\). Other conditional-optimal-transport work supplies covariate-aware identification, observational direct-value rates, or AIPW inference for fitted dual bounds, but not this three-part efficiency-and-coverage result for the sharp smooth primal endpoint. The spectral existence criterion is settled; the remaining inference gap is a full-parent adaptive confidence procedure outside the ruled-out unregularized full-tangent Gaussian route.
fill: The results give the observed-data canonical gradient and efficiency bound, the matching information lower bound, an attaining cross-fitted estimator, the exact signed transport and propensity bias decomposition, a scale-aware variance error of order \(\sigma_n r_{S,n}+r_{S,n}^2+(\sigma_n+r_{S,n})/\sqrt n\), uniform normality and Wald coverage under the three displayed relative-rate conditions, and explicit H\"older phase conditions. These conclusions complement rather than replace earlier smooth COT wavelet inference, observational direct-value estimation, and dual-bound AIPW inference. The note also proves a route-specific equality obstruction: the full-tangent conditional Hessian can contain an infinite-dimensional identity compression and hence be noncompact and non-Hilbert--Schmidt, so uniform unregularized Gaussian spectral calibration is unavailable without covariate-direction regularization or another derivative-aware method.
